title: keyboard remapping

status.label: Needs exact key and repro
status.detail: The report says a function key is not input after remapping but does not identify whether the physical key is Fn or a standard F-key. Keyboard Manager remaps low-level virtual-key events, so the distinction determines whether Windows exposes a remappable event.

next_action: Ask which physical key fails and whether it produces a Windows key event on a current supported build.

judgment.rationale: The original report uses PowerToys 0.97.0 and says a remapped function key produces no input, but it does not name the key, keyboard model, mapped target, or actual/expected result. A July 2026 commenter asked whether the issue persists on 0.100.2 and requested numbered steps; there was no answer. Current Keyboard Manager code looks up mappings from a low-level keyboard event's virtual-key code. If the key is the firmware-level Fn key and Windows receives no distinct key event, PowerToys cannot remap it; a standard F1-F12 key is a different case.
evidence: The open issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-Keyboard Manager; it has no assignee.
The body lists PowerToys 0.97.0 from the Microsoft Store and only says that remapping a function key causes no input.
The single public comment asks whether the issue persists on 0.100.2 and requests numbered steps; it is minimized as low quality and has no author response.
The 2026-10-11 timeline activity only changes product labels; no linked pull request was found.

At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:414-420 handles remaps by looking up the vkCode of a received low-level keyboard event; the report does not establish that Windows exposes the unspecified physical key as a separate event.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the exact physical key, keyboard model, current version, mapped target, and whether Windows observes that key before deciding whether a fix is possible.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix may apply if a standard Windows-visible function key is mishandled, but the issue does not identify the key or confirm that it reaches the low-level keyboard hook.

issue_context.summary: A report says remapping a function key produces no input, but it is unclear whether the key is the hardware Fn key or a standard F-key.
known_information: The reporter lists PowerToys 0.97.0 and Microsoft Store installation.
The report has no named key, keyboard model, mapping target, or expected/actual output.
A July 2026 commenter asked whether the problem persisted on 0.100.2 and requested numbered steps; no reply is present.
Current main handles mappings based on the virtual-key code delivered in a low-level keyboard event.
inferences: A firmware-level Fn key may not be exposed as an independent Windows key event, while a standard F1-F12 key normally enters the Windows keyboard input path; the issue does not identify which case applies.
The observed no-input behavior could also depend on the target mapping or current build.
issue_context.analysis: The next discriminator is the exact physical key and whether it is visible to Windows as a separate key event. Do not request a generic diagnostic bundle or propose a firmware-level fix without knowing whether the source is Fn or F1-F12.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, one public comment, labels, assignees, and timeline through 2026-10-11T16:48:57Z.
Checked for a linked pull request; none was returned by the issue-number search.

information_gaps.information: The exact physical key (Fn versus F1-F12 or another key), keyboard model, mapped target, current PowerToys version, and numbered reproduction.
information_gaps.why_needed: A hardware Fn key may be handled by firmware and produce no separate event for Keyboard Manager, unlike a standard function key.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the keyboard model, exact physical key and target, current PowerToys version, and numbered steps with expected and actual output.

information_gaps.information: Whether Windows or Keyboard Manager's remapping UI detects the physical key with the remap disabled.
information_gaps.why_needed: If the key is not visible as a Windows key event, a PowerToys remap cannot intercept it; if visible, the failure may be in remap handling.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: With Keyboard Manager disabled, check whether pressing the key produces a distinct key in the Windows keyboard/remap UI and report the result.

proposed_fixes.title: Handle Windows-visible function keys consistently
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a standard function key that reaches Windows may not be processed correctly by the selected remap. If the physical key is the firmware-level Fn key and no event reaches Windows, the limitation is outside Keyboard Manager's input path.
plan: Identify the physical key, keyboard model, remap target, and current supported-build behavior.
Confirm that Windows delivers a distinct virtual-key event for the source key, then reproduce with the same mapping.
If a Windows-visible F-key is mishandled, correct the specific mapping path and add a focused regression test; otherwise document the hardware limitation rather than changing the remapper.
verification: A standard Windows-visible function key produces the configured output on the current supported build.
A hardware Fn key that produces no Windows input is not claimed to be fixable by Keyboard Manager.

confidence.rationale: The low-level hook path is known, but the issue does not specify the physical key or whether it produces a Windows event.

actions.label: Approve Windows-visible key investigation
actions.note: Do not design an implementation until the physical key and Windows input event are identified.

actions.label: Request exact key and Windows event

comment.body:
The report says a remapped function key produces no input, but Keyboard Manager can only remap key events Windows delivers. Could you share:
- Whether the physical key is Fn, F1-F12, or another key; the keyboard model; the mapped target; and your current PowerToys version.
- Numbered reproduction steps and whether the remapping UI detects that key when Keyboard Manager is disabled.
This will distinguish a Windows-visible key handling bug from an Fn key handled by the keyboard firmware.
